summary.name: File synchronization
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article explaining file synchronization, the process of keeping files in two or more locations updated under defined rules, with a focus on two-way sync.
use_cases: understanding how two-way file sync works
keeping home backups on external hard drives
updating files for transport on USB flash drives
planning sync topology for several machines
summary.what_it_does: The article defines file synchronization and contrasts one-way mirroring with two-way synchronization. It lists common features of sync systems, including encryption, compression, conflict detection, open-file support, intermediate-device support, change previews, and file diffs. It compares sync with shared file access, noting that sync uses polling agents and supports offline work. It also covers security concerns with consumer sync tools in business settings and the benefits of end-to-end encryption for cloud sync.
notable: Explains star topology for synchronizing multiple machines via a hub
Describes conflict detection and risk of data loss from undetected conflicts
Contrasts sync with shared file access and SyncML-based synchronization
caveats: Article itself is flagged as needing more citations
Synchronized files must physically fit on portable storage when using USB-style sync
